text:
izumi: hey team  joining today! i'm on a corporate Fedora Silverblue image (rpm-ostree) and trying to get a usable dev environment. i prefer using toolbox/podman rather than docker. problems: asdf won't persist installs across toolbox recreates, pip/wheels fail complaining about openssl headers inside the toolbox, ssh-agent forwarding isn't working through a systemd user unit i made, and op signin (1password) only works in my browser extension, not the CLI inside toolbox. any patterns people use for immutable OS + containerized dev? who should i ping for infra quirks?

marta: welcome Izumi! Silverblue is common here, we recommend keeping runtimes inside the toolbox image. For asdf persistence, create a persistent home overlay by bind-mounting ~/.asdf into the toolbox: `podman run -it -v $HOME/.asdf:/home/user/.asdf:Z registry.fedora toolbox` and then in the toolbox `asdf reshim` after installs. Also commit a devtoolbox image with the preinstalled runtimes so you don't reinstall every time.

ryan: about openssl headers: inside toolbox install system deps: `sudo dnf install -y openssl-devel make gcc` (toolbox has sudo). If the project uses musl or different ABIs, ensure the container's distro matches your target. For building wheels, set `export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/usr/lib64/pkgconfig` if pkg-config can't find openssl.

izumi: thanks, i'll try mounting ~/.asdf. question on ssh-agent: i created a systemd --user unit that starts ssh-agent and sets SSH_AUTH_SOCK env in my login session, but when i `podman exec -it toolbox bash` SSH_AUTH_SOCK isn't visible. i symlinked the socket into /run/user but permissions or SELinux might block it.

marta: for sockets with podman, you need the `:Z` chcon label and to bind mount the actual socket into the container: `podman run -v $SSH_AUTH_SOCK:/ssh-agent:Z -e SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent ...` and ensure your user-level ssh-agent socket is world-accessible to the container user (or use a helper that creates a container-scoped socket proxy). Also check `podman run --security-opt label=disable` for testing to rule out SELinux.

ryan: alternative is to use `socat` proxy on host to expose a minimal forwarded socket the container can use, avoiding sharing full GNUPG or ssh directories. We have a small repo `infra/ssh-proxy` in the onboarding repo.

izumi: op signin weirdness: extension works in browser but `op` CLI inside toolbox gives `you must be signed in` after pasting browser output. is there a way to use the browser session inside toolbox?

marta: browser extension sessions aren't automatically visible to the CLI. Use `op signin --raw` in a host shell and write the token to a file, then mount into toolbox as `OP_SESSION_my`. Example: `op signin my --raw > ~/.op_session && podman run -v $HOME/.op_session:/tmp/op_session:Z -e OP_SESSION_my=$(cat ~/.op_session) ...` Or use ephemeral `op` token via `op account add --interactive` inside toolbox.

devex-bot: FYI onboarding note for Silverblue/toolbox patterns: https://intranet.redwood/dev-setup/silverblue-toolbox  includes asdf persistence examples, podman socket mounts, and op CLI tips.

izumi: awesome, that doc link should help. last question: i'd like commit signing with gpg but don't want keys in the toolbox. can i forward gpg-agent similarly to ssh?

ryan: yes, same idea: mount the agent socket (usually at `/run/user/1000/gnupg/S.gpg-agent`) into the container with `:Z` label and set `GNUPGHOME` accordingly. prefer a socket proxy approach so you don't inadvertently expose the whole GNUPGHOME. security will want readonly mounts and strict selinux labels.

infra-bot: Hi Izumi  infra note: corporate Silverblue images have a default SELinux policy that blocks certain host socket mounts by default. If you need a permanent exception for your workstation to bind the ssh/gpg sockets into containers, open REQ-2168 and include your hostname. For temporary access, request a short-lived policy relax via DM to @ryan.

izumi: thanks everyone  mounting ~/.asdf into toolbox, installing openssl-devel inside toolbox, and using mounted OP_SESSION token all worked. i'll follow up with infra on the SELinux exception if needed. i'll also open a PR to the onboarding repo with a short Silverblue checklist. appreciate the help :smile:
